extracted.intended_audience: researchers applying for the ERC Proof of Concept (PoC) grant; current or recent ERC grantees
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation criteria and process for the European Research Council (ERC) Proof of Concept Grant: a single-sentence 'Excellence' criterion broken down into three elements (Breakthrough Innovation Potential; Approach and Methodology; Strategic Leadership and Project Management), assessed by external experts. Includes eligibility restrictions that applicants must be current or recent ERC grantees and build on results from an existing/completed ERC project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sole Evaluation Criterion: Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Proof of Concept Grant is evaluated based on the sole criterion of excellence, which comprises three evaluation elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The three evaluation elements are: Breakthrough Innovation Potential; Approach and Methodology; Strategic Leadership and Project Management. All three elements must be passed by a majority of experts for funding eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breakthrough Innovation Potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must demonstrate that the proposed Proof of Concept activity has the potential to drive innovation and business inventiveness and/or tackle societal challenges, and that the proposed expected outcomes are innovative or distinctive compared to existing solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment focuses on how the PoC activity could lead to innovation or address societal challenges, and whether expected outcomes are novel/distinct relative to current solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach and Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed Proof of Concept activities and planning are feasible within the proposed timescales and resources, and are appropriate and effective to explore the pathway from ground-breaking research towards innovation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluators judge feasibility (timescale, resources) and whether the planned activities are suitable and effective for progressing from research results to innovation/commercialisation pathways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Leadership and Project Management
rubrics_metrics.description: This element concerns the researcher's strategic leadership and project management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment considers the principal investigator/researcher's ability to provide strategic direction and to manage the project effectively to achieve the PoC objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Process and Scoring / Pass Threshold
rubrics_metrics.description: External experts mark each element on a three-level scale: Very good; Good; Fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible for funding, a proposal must receive a pass (either 'very good' or 'good') from a majority of experts on all three evaluation elements. A 'fail' on any element by a majority prevents funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility (applicant and project provenance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PoC Grant is open only to current or recent ERC grantees, and the activities must build on results from an existing or completed ERC project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is a precondition: only applicants who are current or recent ERC grant holders and whose PoC activities derive from previous ERC-funded research may apply.
